title: The Price of Defying Heaven
next_chapter_hook: When that blood-red figure blocked before him, trading life for life in an instant, Chen Ji finally understood what it meant to have his heart ripped apart.

text.content: The void trembled, Chen Ji's roar still echoing when the voice of the Fate Scribe sliced into his ears like an ice blade. "The second path?" He gritted his teeth, every word seeming to be carved from his chest, "Let me see then, this so-called second path, how much better can it be!" His fingertips dug deep into his palms, blood dripping through his fingers, yet he noticed nothing. Twelve years of endurance, twelve years of scheming, twelve years of careful advancement—Chen Ji never fought without preparation, but now, for the first time, he felt genuine fear. Not fear of death, but fear of that unknown "price."

The words fell, and the void twisted abruptly. A grand vision unfurled before Chen Ji's eyes like a scroll—above the heavens, countless stars arranged in formation, the galaxy inverted like a waterfall, immortal light cascading down like a torrent. And upon the vast earth, dense black banners blotted out the sky, the great banner bearing the character "Holy" fluttering violently in the wild wind. The demonic army, a million-strong, converging into a black ocean that stretched beyond sight. Chen Ji saw himself standing at the highest point, clad in black battle armor, eyes burning with rage sufficient to incinerate the heavens. Behind him, Ye Qing stood in a crimson dress atop the summit of ten thousand demons, demonic energy coiling around her like a tornado. She turned to look at him, a meaningful smile curling at her lips. "This battle, we've waited far too long for."

dialogue.content: "The second path, defy heaven and strike against the Dao." The Fate Scribe's voice came from all directions, cold and mechanical. "You shall ally with the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, using the million demonic army as blade, the living world as sacrifice, to wage war against the heavens. You will win. You will personally shatter the immortal gates that stand above mortals. You will become the new sovereign—but the price is, you must personally slaughter all who fought beside you." A pause, and that voice carried a strange delight. "All your allies, friends, beloved... they are all sacrificial offerings required in this war. If you do not slaughter them all, you cannot break the shackles of fate."

text.content: The vision flowed. Chen Ji saw himself standing atop mountains of corpses and rivers of blood, his sword still dripping. At his feet lay countless familiar faces—those who had supported him in the shadows, those who had shared wine with him, those who had sworn to follow him unto death. Their eyes were wide open,死不瞑目, as if asking: Why? Chen Ji felt a violent vertigo, his stomach churning, nearly heaving. "No..." His voice was hoarse, barely audible, "This is impossible... there must be another way..." But the vision didn't stop, continuing ruthlessly to display that blood-soaked path. War, death, endless slaughter—and his own face, cold as a demon god.

Han Lie! The vision froze abruptly. Chen Ji saw Han Lie kneeling in blood-soaked ground, this strongest genius of the Xuanwu Sect now wretched and pathetic, this堂堂spirit transformation境great cultivator had his legs shattered. He looked up at Chen Ji, his eyes holding none of the old arrogance and disdain, only deep fear and confusion. "Why..." Han Lie struggled to speak, "I thought... at least we were opponents..." Chen Ji saw himself in the vision walking closer slowly, sword tip pressing against Han Lie's throat. "Opponent?" He heard himself coldly laugh, "You dare claim that?" Sword light flashed, Han Lie's head rolled to the ground, the final resentment in his eyes still not fading. Chen Ji felt as if someone had stabbed a knife into his chest—that was someone he killed personally— even if a sworn enemy, it was still a living life!

Ye Qing! The vision shifted again. Chen Ji saw Ye Qing standing alone at the cliff's edge, crimson dress fluttering wildly in the wind, vast demonic energy forming a pair of sky-blocking black wings behind her. She turned to face Chen Ji, eyes full of resolve and release. "Chen Ji, this path... was something you forced upon me." Her voice was soft, yet clearly entered Chen Ji's ears, "Since death is inevitable, let me... choose how to die." Before the words finished, she forcefully activated her internal demonic arts—self-destruction! In the earth-shaking explosion, Ye Qing's figure turned into scattered blood mist, leaving only a soft sigh echoing in the void. "If there's an afterlife... I don't want to meet you again." Chen Ji's knees slammed heavily to the ground, that sigh like a venomous snake drilling into his heart, gnawing at every inch of flesh.

Heaven and Earth in Mourning! The vision pulled back sharply. Chen Ji saw the entire world collapsing. The three great sects turned to ruins, countless billions of innocent lives reduced to dust in war. A massive crack split open the heavens, endless chaos qi pouring down, swallowing the entire world. He saw Su Qingyao clutching a swaddled infant, desperately kneeling in the ruins; saw Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul wailing and dissipating in the flames; saw that old fox Ling Yuan finally reveal his true face, yet at the same moment consumed by chaos. And he himself, standing atop the ruins of heaven and earth, as lonely as an ancient unchanging stone, his eyes holding nothing but emptiness. He gained freedom, yet lost the entire world. He gained everything, yet lost everything.

dialogue.content: "This is the second path." The Fate Scribe's voice rang out again, devoid of any emotion, "Defy heaven and strike the Dao, use the living world as sacrifice, slaughter all loved ones, only then can you break free from the shackles. You will possess the power to reshape heaven and earth, yet will become a true solitary ruler." A sinister laughter echoed through the void, "Interestingly, countless seers have chosen this path. They say it's the fastest, most direct method. After all... killing others is always easier than killing oneself, isn't it?" Chen Ji knelt on the ground, trembling violently, yet could not utter a single word. He had thought himself omniscient, calculating all under heaven, but now he discovered he could calculate nothing.

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, eyes radiating unprecedented light. "Both paths are dead ends?" He laughed, the laughter growing louder, finally turning into a skyward howl, "Good! Excellent! Since you want me to choose, let me tell you—Chen Ji never plays according to another's chess manual!" He struggled to stand, his entire aura changing dramatically. The edge that had been suppressed for twelve years, at this moment, erupted like a volcanic eruption. The void trembled; for the first time, the Fate Scribe's voice showed a tremor: "You... what are you going to do?"

text.content: Chen Ji's body seemed drained of all strength, crashing to the ground on his knees. His hands braced against the void, knuckles white, his entire body trembling violently. "I killed Ye Qing... I killed everyone..." His voice was fragmented, eyes full of despair and self-loathing, "Is this still me? Is this still me!" He let out a near-mad howl, tears streaming down his face. The Fate Scribe let out a meaningful light laugh: "This is the real you, Chen Ji. Everyone thinks they're the protagonist, but in the end... they're nothing but puppets manipulated by fate." Those虚无eyes seemed to mock his powerlessness.

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions. His gaze gradually regained clarity. Though his voice still trembled, every word was crystal clear: "You mentioned two paths... there's a third one, isn't there?" The Void fell into brief silence. The Fate Chronicler didn't answer immediately. Chen Ji saw hope, his lips curving into a cold sneer: "You deliberately only showed me these two paths because the Third Path—is what you truly fear, right?" His fingers tapped lightly against the Void, as if calculating something, "So you use these blood-soaked scenes to shake my Dao heart, because you know... if I truly calm down, you'll find—you can't trap me at all."

In the Void, the atmosphere turned bizarre. The Fate Chronicler fell silent. That mechanical, ice-cold voice carried for the first time a hint of... wariness? "You're very clever, Chen Ji. Cleverer than any of the previous prophets." After a long while, that voice resumed, "But clever people often die faster." Chen Ji felt an invisible pressure suddenly descend upon him, as if the entire heavens and earth were rejecting him. His Heavenly Fate Value plummeted, the Tianji Record Fragment trembled violently, seemingly issuing some kind of warning. But he didn't retreat. Instead, he walked forward step by step against that pressure. "The more you intimidate me, the more it proves I guessed correctly." His voice grew colder, "The Third Path... what exactly is it?"

Just then, another vision emerged. But this time, it wasn't war, wasn't slaughter—a scene Chen Ji had never seen before. It was a chaotic Void, and at its center floated an eye. That eye was too massive, large enough to shroud half the firmament; it was too brilliant, shining like a burning star, impossible to look upon directly. Chen Ji instinctively lowered his head, a profound fear rising in his heart—a trembling from the depths of his soul. "That is the Eye of Heavenly Dao." The Fate Chronicler's voice sounded, "The 'will of Heavenly Dao' you speak of, the ultimate villain you imagine..." Pausing, the voice turned meaningful, "Did you think it was merely an enemy to be slain? Naive. It's not an enemy, Chen Ji—it is the Rule itself."

Chen Ji猛地抬头，瞳孔骤缩。规则？天道是规则？他的大脑飞速运转，无数念头在脑海中碰撞。天道之眼不是生物，而是规则……那么所谓的'逆天伐道'，本质上是……"你要打破的不是某个存在，而是规则本身。"他murmured自语，"所以无论第一条路还是第二条路，都是在规则之内行事——要么顺从，要么毁灭……但这两条路，都无法真正触及规则的核心！"他感到自己的思路豁然开朗，但与此同时，一股更深的寒意也涌上心头。如果天道是规则，那他要挑战的，就是这个世界最基本的运行法则……这真的可能吗？

text.content: Chen Ji's voice echoed through the Void, carrying unwavering resolve: "Show me the Third Path." The Fate Chronicler fell silent. That silence lasted so long Chen Ji thought the other would never speak again. Then that voice returned, carrying a strange sigh: "Are you certain you want to see?" Chen Ji gave no answer, but his straight spine spoke volumes. "Very well." The Fate Chronicler's voice grew low, "Since you insist on seeking death... I shall show you what true hell looks like." In the Void, a crack slowly tore open, revealing an even deeper, more terrifying darkness.

Through the crack, visions began to emerge. Chen Ji saw a familiar figure—himself, yet not himself. That "Chen Ji" stood in ruins, surrounded by no enemies, no allies—only endless Void and eternal silence. He saw that "Chen Ji" slowly raise his head, his face utterly expressionless, his eyes holding no hatred, no anger, not even sorrow—only a deathly, hollow emptiness. "Is this the Third Path?" Chen Ji's voice tightened, "What is this...?" He felt an inexplicable terror. Compared to the blood-soaked horror of the first two paths, this path's "tranquility" was even more chilling.

The Fate Chronicler's voice sounded again, this time with rare seriousness: "The Third Path is Transcendence." In the vision, that "Chen Ji" slowly raised his hand, and in his palm manifested a fragmented ancient tome—the Tianji Record, yet not the fragment Chen Ji currently possessed, but... the Complete Tianji Record. "When you truly see through the truth of fate, when you are no longer bound by any emotion, when you..." The Fate Chronicler's voice suddenly became evasive, as if deliberately avoiding something, "...make that choice, you will obtain the Complete Tianji Record. Then, you will possess the power to rewrite the Rule. But the price is—" The vision abruptly twisted. That "Chen Ji"'s figure began dissolving, merging into the Void as countless motes of light. Chen Ji saw within those motes countless flashes—countless "Chen Jis," countless endings, remnants of countless paths.

The vision completely dissolved, leaving only nothingness. Chen Ji stood in place, his mind racing. The Third Path... Transcendence? Abandoning emotions? Making a choice? He vaguely grasped something, yet it slipped away. "You're deliberately being vague." He coldly smiled, "What are you afraid of?" The Fate Chronicler gave no answer. After a long silence, that voice finally sounded, carrying a subtle warning: "Chen Ji, I have already given you enough hints. The remaining path must be walked by yourself." Pausing, the voice turned meaningful, "But remember, no matter which path you choose... the Fate Chronicler will be waiting at the end." As the words fell, the Void began collapsing. A powerful repulsive force sent Chen Ji hurtling out.

Chen Ji's eyes snapped open. He found himself still standing at the Cliff Edge of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. The night wind was biting, whipping his robes. It was as if that entire dialogue with the Fate Chronicler had merely been an illusory dream. But he knew it wasn't—he tightly gripped the Tianji Record Fragment in his hand, his palm slick with cold sweat. He lowered his gaze to the fragment, discovering its inscriptions had become even more blurred than before, as if something was being slowly extracted. "The Third Path..." he murmured to himself, a complex light flickering in his eyes, "Transcendence, abandoning emotions, making a choice..." He suddenly recalled something, sharply lifting his head to gaze toward the horizon. The gears of fate had begun turning, and he—must find the answer before that moment arrives.

Just then, a crimson figure streaked across the distant horizon like a meteor, plunging toward the cliff below. Chen Ji's pupils constricted—that crimson was too familiar, familiar enough to make his heart seize. He urged his body forward, darting down at speed. The night wind howled in his ears. He saw on the platform below the cliff, as the pervasive demonic energy dissipated, a red-clothed figure lay in a pool of blood. Ye Qing! Chen Ji felt his mind explode. An unprecedented terror and fury surged through him. A longsword pierced her chest, its hilt bearing the emblem of the Xuanwu Sect—that was Han Lie's sword! At this moment, Ye Qing's aura was rapidly fading. She lifted her head, using her final strand of strength to gaze at Chen Ji, a pale yet serene smile curving her lips: "Finally... found you..." Blood spilled from her lips, dyeing half her cheek crimson, yet still breathtakingly beautiful. "This time... let me... protect you..."
